chunks: With this chain of narrators, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan ibn Bint Ilyas, who said: I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of Allah (Allah's blessings be upon him and his Family) said:
May Allah curse the one who performs a sin or gives refuge to a sinner. I said: And what is the sin? He said: The one who murders.

key_terms.آوَى: To give refuge or shelter to
key_terms.حَدَث: A sin or deed, specifically interpreted here as murder

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'hadath' (sin) in this hadith from Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) provides a specific exegetical clarification of the term 'hadath' (newly invented matter/sin) as used in the Prophet's hadith, narrowing its scope in this context to murder. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of using the Imams' interpretations to resolve ambiguities in prophetic traditions, highlighting the gravity of bloodshed as a primordial sin. The definition underscores the legal and spiritual weight of homicide within the broader framework of divine curses.

en.basel-kadem: 6.	With this chain of narrators, from Hussain bin Sa’eed, from Hasan, son of the daughter of Ilyas, that he said: I heard al-Rida, peace be upon him, say: The Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said:
May Allah curse the one who performs a sin or gives refuge to a sinner. I said: And what is the sin? He said: The one who murders.
